text:
Avery: Kicking off the all-hands follow-up thread — drop questions about mission, positioning, market, or competitors here. I’ll answer high-level and loop in folks who can add details. :hand:
Priya: Quick one — how tight is our messaging vs "platform" players? Do we lead with performance/cost or flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private)? :thinking:
Mateo: Short answer: we lean performance+economics for engineers, flexibility for enterprise buy. Operational reliability is the tie-breaker when customers compare us to big cloud APIs.
Sanjay: Follow-up for Mateo — any guidance on which roadmap items map to the performance message? e.g., kernel selection + caching improvements vs product features.
Mateo: Kernel and caching are core proof points for the performance story. On the product side, streaming, function-calling, and predictable latency are what we show in demos. We should include microbench numbers in the pitch.
Olivia: For marketing — do we have permission to say "price-sensitive production workloads" in external decks? Want the exact phrasing to avoid sounding discounting.
Avery: Prefer: "cost-aware, production-grade inference" — emphasizes both economics and reliability without sounding cheap. Use that line in slides.
Jenna: On Dedicated vs Private: some customers ask "why pick Dedicated over Private if security/compliance is the ask?" How do we advise SDRs?
Kieran: From sales: customers often choose Dedicated for predictable throughput + isolation without onboarding private infra. Private is for stricter networking/KMS or air-gapped needs. Price and lead time are bigger diffs.
Avery: Exactly. Dedicated = turnkey capacity + SLA. Private = full control + compliance. We should add a one-pager for AE enablement. Jenna can you own that?
Jenna: Yep, will draft and share by EOD Thursday.
Sanjay: Curious about competitors — which specific vendors should eng call out when customers compare latencies? We get asked about BigCloud and ModelCo in proofs.
Mateo: Call out typical comparisons: BigCloud endpoint latencies (variable), ModelCo self-hosted (high ops overhead), and Infravendor runtimes (good latency but less integrated platform). Use concrete numbers where we have benchmarks.
Olivia: Can we get a short stat for the marketing kit? e.g., "X% lower latency than BigCloud on 2k tokens on A100" — need numbers we can source.
Sanjay: We have internal perf slides — RudderBot, can you paste the all-hands perf slide link?
RudderBot: Here are the slides: https://slides.example.com/redwood/all-hands-mar-2026 — perf deck is slide 12-18.
Avery: On the market thesis — reminder we position inference as the operating layer where teams compete on cost+latency+reliability. That helps explain why model ownership matters less than serving. Use that when asked about models vs serving.
Priya: Is our messaging intentionally agnostic to specific model names? Some customers ask if we "endorse" hosting vendor models.
Avery: We curate a model catalog but don’t exclusively endorse a single model. Messaging: "Model-agnostic serving with Redwood-verified performance profiles."
Kieran: Pricing question from an AE — when do we pitch reserved pricing vs usage-based?
Mateo: Reserved (Dedicated) when they need predictable throughput or want committed discounts. Usage-based for evaluation and early PLG adoption.
Olivia: I'll update external assets with the suggested lines. Can someone drop a short one-liner about the thesis we can use on the homepage?
Avery: Use: "Redwood makes high-performance, reliable LLM inference predictable and economical for engineering teams." Short and to the point.
Sanjay: One last ops question — any changes to the SLA language we should expect this quarter?
Avery: Slight tightening for Dedicated SLAs in Q2. Legal will circulate redlines next week.
Priya: Thanks! small ask — can leadership post a bullet summary after the thread so AEs and marketing have an official copy? :pray:
Avery: Will post a short summary and link to the one-pager Jenna produces. Thanks all — keep the questions coming and tag me if it’s urgent. :rocket:
